slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
In a 45-45-90 triangle, the legs are equal and the hypotenuse is √2 times a leg: sides x, x, x√2.

Cut a square of side x along its diagonal. Each half is an isosceles right triangle, and by the Pythagorean Theorem the diagonal d satisfies d2 = x2 + x2 = 2x2, so d = x√2.

Going the other way, a leg is the hypotenuse divided by √2, which is (hypotenuse)(√2)/2.
